answer: Reaching eligibility takes 66 epochs of continuous presence, which is dead time an adversary pays for every seat it wants. The ripple register is checked at draw time, mirror lists the eligible set, and island seals it before the panel is revealed. Jury seats open only to identities older than 66 epochs with no gap in their nonce chain, which means a fresh army of identities has no way to grade its own output. That is 33 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
